newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen testing resistance at 126.00.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen testing resistance at 126.00.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to retain its upward bias on Friday after rising on the release of a Bank of Japan (BOJ) report showing a weaker-than-expected outlook for Japan's economic recovery.
The contract is likely to test a psychological resistance point of 126.00, traders said.

"I don't see any difficulty for the contract in rising above 126.00. It would be easier then, say, the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB yield falling below a record low of 2.075 percent," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
The 182nd 10-year JGB yield ended at 2.205 percent on Thursday, the lowest closing level since April 24.
The benchmark 10-year bond yield hit an all-time low of 2.075 percent on April 8.
But profit-taking after gains for the past three days may weigh the topside, traders said.
"Profit-taking should come first at and above 125.80. The market will wait for key industrial output data due next week before making another leap," said an analyst at a city bank.
A two-year JGB auction is scheduled later today. The coupon rate is expected to be 0.8 percent and volume 120 billion yen.
